merger_name: Waveconn - acquisition of certain Optus towers and sites

acquirers.name: Waveconn Infrastructure Pty Ltd as trustee of the Waveconn Infrastructure Trust

party_page.name: Waveconn Infrastructure Pty Ltd as trustee of the Waveconn Infrastructure Trust

merger_description:
Waveconn Infrastructure Pty Ltd as trustee of the Waveconn Infrastructure Trust (**Waveconn**) proposes to acquire 42 Optus sites (designated as **Deferred Sites**) from Optus Mobile Pty Ltd (**Optus**) under a Tower Asset Transfer Agreement. The Tower Asset Transfer Agreement is a broader agreement that was entered into in September 2025.   

  

The Waveconn Group is a provider of neutral-host telecommunications infrastructure in Australia, supplying bespoke and standard telecommunication structures and associated infrastructure for co-location. Waveconn currently owns and operates a passive neutral-host digital infrastructure portfolio of towers, building rooftops and wireless infrastructure assets across Australia.   

  

Waveconn was formed through OMERS’ acquisition of the TPG/Vodafone tower and rooftop portfolio and Stilmark. Waveconn operates independently, with no direct or indirect mobile network operator ownership or funding.   

  

The Deferred Sites are mainly mobile coverage sites co-funded by Government. Their sale forms part of Optus’ broader strategy to focus on service provision rather than passive infrastructure ownership. The Deferred Sites comprise the site tenure, tower or rooftop structures and associated passive infrastructure.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. the increase in share of mobile passive infrastructure sites
arising from the Acquisition would be very small
b. there are alternative suppliers of passive wireless
telecommunications infrastructure in Australia
c. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
effects resulting from exclusionary conduct post-acquisition,
including due to the operation of the Facilities Access Code.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
